claims.text: Controlled solidification followed by thermomechanical processing creates a hierarchical microstructure in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The resulting hierarchical microstructure simultaneously increases strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
The hierarchical microstructure contains refined grains and an optimized phase distribution.
Grain refinement and optimization of phase distribution increase strength.
The hierarchical microstructure reduces stress concentrations.
The hierarchical microstructure increases resistance to dislocation movement.
Grain-boundary sliding and twinning provide additional deformation pathways that improve ductility.
Dislocation accumulation and interaction with grain boundaries increase strain hardening.
The proposed mechanisms make deformation more homogeneous and delay necking.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by 30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The intervention is expected to work at ambient and elevated temperatures and across various strain rates.
The intervention is expected to be effective in eutectic high-entropy alloys containing a mixture of FCC and BCC phases.
AlCoCrFeNi is an example of the proposed mixed-FCC/BCC alloy class.
CoCrFeMnNi is an example of the proposed mixed-FCC/BCC alloy class.
The magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition, processing parameters, and testing conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvements are 20% in yield strength and 30% in elongation, but the operational falsification rule ultimately requires only 15% improvement in each property. Results between 15% and the respective predicted values would fail to meet the prediction but would not falsify it under the stated 1.15-times criterion.

The rule first combines a 15% minimum with a requirement that both properties meet the predicted 20% and 30% improvements, but then states that the specific requirement is only 1.15 times baseline for both properties.
